Claim denials, partial payments, and delays are common problems with health insurance reimbursement in India, leaving many policyholders financially and mentally stressed. A 2024 survey by LocalCircles found that 43% of policyholders struggled with claims over the previous three years. 
Common reasons for claim rejection

Non-disclosure of pre-existing diseases (PED): This is a leading cause of claim rejection. Failure to accurately disclose medical history when purchasing a policy can lead to denied claims later on.

Waiting period violations: Most health policies have waiting periods for specific diseases, pre-existing conditions, or the initial period after purchase. Filing a claim during this time will lead to rejection.

Incorrect or incomplete information: Providing inaccurate details on claim forms or missing documents is a frequent reason for denial.

Policy exclusions: Claims for treatments or conditions that are specifically excluded from your policy's coverage will be rejected. This can include certain cosmetic procedures, alternative treatments, and specific therapies.

Lapsed policy: If your policy is not renewed on time, any claim filed while it is expired will be rejected.

Exhaustion of sum insured: A claim will be denied if the policy's coverage amount has been fully exhausted by previous claims within the same policy year.

Insufficient hospitalization: If the insurer determines that hospitalization was not medically necessary, the claim may be rejected.

Role of Artificial Intelligence AI in Cardiology.  AI in cardiology enhances patient care by automating image analysis, improving diagnostic accuracy, and predicting risks for conditions like heart failure and arrhythmias. It enables rapid interpretation of ECGs and echocardiograms, often exceeding human efficiency in identifying hidden cardiac issues. Key roles include, but are not limited to: 
Imaging & Diagnosis: AI automates segmentation of cardiac structures, analyzes echocardiograms, and identifies coronary plaque from CT scans faster than manual analysis.
Predictive Analytics: Algorithms analyze large datasets to identify high-risk patients for heart failure rehospitalization, arrhythmias, and stroke, enabling earlier, tailored interventions.
Remote Monitoring & Wearables: AI-driven Apple Watch apps detect low ventricular ejection fraction and irregular rhythms in real-time, aiding early diagnosis of heart disease.
Improved Efficiency: By reducing the time spent on manual data interpretation and EHR documentation, AI allows clinicians to focus on personalized, patient-centered care. 
AI serves as a powerful, non-invasive, and increasingly accurate tool, transforming cardiovascular medicine from reactive to proactive, particularly in detecting subtle abnormalities such as left ventricular dysfunction.

What's Coronary Calcium Score?
A coronary calcium score (or Calcium Score Test) is a non-invasive, CT-scan-based test that measures the amount of calcified plaque in the coronary arteries. By detecting this hardened plaque, it helps estimate the risk of developing coronary artery disease (CAD) and heart attacks, usually for people with intermediate risk factors. 
What the Score Means (Agatston Score)
0: No detectable calcium, indicating very low risk of a heart attack.
1–99: Mild plaque buildup.
100–300: Moderate plaque buildup, indicating high risk of coronary artery disease.
>300: Extensive plaque burden and very high risk of heart attack. 
Key Aspects of the Test
Purpose: Identifies early, silent atherosclerosis before symptoms occur, aiding in decisions regarding lifestyle changes or statin therapy.
Procedure: A quick, painless CT scan of the heart that takes about 10–15 minutes.
Limitations: It measures plaque, not blockages, and does not show non-calcified (soft) plaque.
Radiation: The test involves a small amount of radiation, similar to 23 chest x-rays on average. 
It is primarily used as a predictive tool, not a diagnostic tool for immediate heart blockage.

What is CIMT?
Carotid Intima-Media Thickness (CIMT) measured by ultrasound is a valuable, non-invasive tool for detecting early-stage atherosclerosis, acting as a surrogate marker for systemic vascular disease, including Coronary Artery Disease (CAD). Increased CIMT indicates underlying atherosclerosis, correlating with cardiovascular risk factors, the severity of CAD, and future cardiovascular events, helping to identify individuals at higher risk and guide treatment for better outcomes. 

How CIMT Detects CAD

Early Atherosclerosis Marker: CIMT quantifies the thickening of the inner layers (intima and media) of the carotid artery wall, a sign of subclinical atherosclerosis before symptoms appear.

Correlation with CAD Severity: Studies show a direct relationship: the thicker the CIMT, the more extensive the coronary artery involvement (e.g., single, double, or triple-vessel disease).

Risk Stratification: High CIMT, along with plaque presence, helps identify patients with increased risk for heart attack, stroke, and other cardiovascular events, refining risk assessment beyond traditional factors. 

What CIMT Measures

Measurement: It's the distance between the first bright line (lumen-intima) and the second bright line (media-adventitia) on high-resolution ultrasound of the common carotid artery.

Normal vs. Elevated: Values typically range from ~0.5 to ~0.9 mm, but increase with age, with higher values suggesting more disease.

Leadless pacemaker is a tiny, self-contained capsule—roughly 90% smaller than traditional devices—implanted directly into the heart to treat slow heart rates without wires (leads) or a chest pocket. It offers a minimally invasive, catheter-based solution with fewer long-term complications, such as infections or lead failures. 

Key Advantages of Leadless Pacemakers:

No Leads or Surgical Pocket: By eliminating wires, it removes risks of lead fracture, dislodgement, and associated infections. There is no, under-the-skin, "pocket" or incision in the chest.

Minimally Invasive Procedure: Inserted via a catheter through the femoral vein (leg), resulting in a faster procedure, minimal scarring, and quicker recovery.

Cosmetic and Physical Comfort: The device is invisible, causing no, under-the-skin, lump on the chest. Patients feel no physical discomfort while moving.

Fewer Activity Restrictions: Due to the absence of wire, patients often face fewer restrictions on upper body movement after the initial healing period.

MRI Compatibility: These devices are designed to be safe for use in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) machines.

Long-Lasting: The device has a long battery life, typically lasting 10–15 years. 

Leadless pacemakers are particularly beneficial for patients with high infection risks, vascular issues (e.g., dialysis patients), or prior device-related complications.

I have been consulting Dr. Dhiren Shah for my father, who has been undergoing treatment for a heart condition for the past two years. We had been visiting this doctor regularly for about a year, and during almost every visit, tests such as ECG and 2D Echo were conducted.

Based on the reports, Dr. Shah informed us that my father’s condition had significantly worsened and that he might have suffered a silent heart attack, resulting in damage to his heart. When we confronted the doctor about this serious mistake, he attempted to take the file from us, apparently to remove the incorrect report. We refused to hand it over. Instead of acknowledging the error and addressing our concerns, he asked us to leave the clinic, became argumentative, used inappropriate language, and repeatedly changed his statements regarding the incident.

In my opinion, mixing up patient reports and altering medications based on another person’s medical records is an extremely serious matter that can put a patient’s health at risk. I am sharing this experience so that others can make informed decisions regarding their healthcare.

Dr. Sandeep is not just a surgeon  he’s a healer blessed with the steady hands of Lord Narayana and the wisdom of Mata Saraswati.

I’m writing this straight from the heart  a long note filled with gratitude for Dr. Sandeep Honnekeri, who quite literally gave my father a second life under his care at Breach Candy Hospital,

Sandeep sir performed the latest beating heart surgery with LIMA RIMA Y Grafts &  coronary endarterectomy on 24th October 2025 for my father.

Our journey to find the right surgeon for my 75 year old father was nothing short of a roller coaster. He was diagnosed with triple-vessel coronary artery disease, with severe diffuse calcification and total occlusions (100% LAD, 100% RCA, 90% LCx and Ramus), and his ejection fraction was just 40%. Though he could still move around, he had lost a lot of muscle mass making the surgery even riskier.

We must have visited nearly every top CVTS doctor in Mumbai the big names everyone talks about. But what we saw was disappointing. Many doctors were performing 3-4 surgeries a day, and it almost felt like my father is just a part of their numbers game. What truly matters in such cases is not speed or PR, but attention to detail. Some doctors didn’t even bother to physically check my father they just looked at the angiography CD & gave an opinion. A few were in such a hurry to admit him that they handed over cost estimates on the first meeting. Some sent their junior assistants to take history while they attended conferences.

It was frustrating and disheartening until we met Dr. Sandeep Honnekeri, who was strongly referred to us by a relative who happens to be one of his old patient. He was the only one who carefully went through every report, took time to physically examine my father, and discussed the risks and approach in detail before making a decision. He’s also someone open to new ideas & research. He is humble enough to put the patient’s well-being before his own ego or status. Breach Candy Hospital is truly lucky to have him.

What impressed us most was how involved he was in every single step right from surgery to dressing changes. He doesn’t delegate critical work to assistants, and that’s rare these days. The respect his team and nurses have for him says a lot. And beyond his skills, he has this calm, reassuring presence he never dismisses even the smallest or silliest question. He listens, explains with logic, and often lightens up tense moments with humour. He will treat you like a son or daughter & not like patient’s relative.

We can never thank him enough. We wish him great health & long life so that he continues to heal & give hope to many more families like ours.

You are truly the best in class sir.
Thank you from the bottom of our hearts.

featured_reviews.name: Bankim Chauhan

My Experience with Dr. Sandeep Honnekeri – Cardiac Surgeon

I want to express my deepest gratitude and appreciation for Dr. Sandeep Honnekeri, who performed an Aortic Valve Replacement + CABG on my 62-year-old brother-in-law. Our interaction with him was extensive — pre-surgery, during surgery, and throughout a month-long ICU stay. Here’s why he stands apart:

1. Exceptional Pre-Surgery Counseling
Dr. Honnekeri took time to thoroughly understand my brother-in-law’s cardiac issues along with other clinical conditions. What truly helped was his counseling — he explained the risks, procedure, and post-op expectations to us relatives in clear, layman’s language. There were no rushed consultations. We went into surgery informed and reassured.

2. Team Introduction & Transparency
He personally introduced us to his surgical and anesthesia team. That small gesture built immense trust and eased our anxiety.

3. One-to-One ICU Management
Post-surgery, his commitment was extraordinary. For nearly a month in ICU, Dr. Honnekeri managed my brother-in-law one-to-one. Every day, he updated us on the progress, explained the day’s plan, and patiently walked us through lab and radiology reports. No question was too small.

4. Real-Time Communication
Whether it was steady recovery or unexpected developments, he informed us in real time — with honesty and empathy. We never felt left in the dark.

5. Hands-On Approach
Despite being a senior cardiac surgeon, he believes in doing every task himself — from minor dressings to suture removal and bedside procedures. That level of personal care is rare after major surgery.

6. Handling Unrelated Complications
During the ICU stay, two major medical incidents occurred unrelated to the heart surgery. Dr. Honnekeri not only predicted and identified them early, but addressed them swiftly. This vigilance likely saved my brother-in-law’s life.

Above all, Dr. Honnekeri’s interactions are humble, motivational, and healing. He treats the patient and the family. In the most stressful month of our lives, he was not just a surgeon but a pillar of strength.

Our family will forever be indebted to him. If you’re looking for a cardiac surgeon who combines surgical excellence with genuine compassion, Dr. Sandeep Honnekeri is the one.

I suffered a "silent heart attack" in late April, and approached our known cardiac specialist.

After angio, it was discovered that I had 6 major blockages in multiple arteries that supply blood to heart muscles.

Dr Honnekeri was recommended along with several other leading cardiac surgeons in Mumbai area. We approached Dr Honnekeri as my elder brother had previously consulted with him and felt he was the right choice for us.

From the first meeting itself, I felt very comfortable with Dr Honnekeri, and the surgery approach that he was recommending.

He clearly explained my Angio results to me, and helped me understand what would be done during the surgery and the post-operative care that would be required.

Under his recommendation we scheduled the surgery at Breach Candy and proceeded with it.

The surgery was done extremely well, he kept my family informed on progress through the day, and when I was back in ICU, I was not only comfortable but looking forward to full recovery. Throughout that day he was checking with ICU staff every couple hours on my progress. If I can say he was connected the whole day with staff, not to mention the 8+ hours of actual surgery time. He has a tremendous work ethic and does not leave things to chance or subordinates!

After a week's stay in ICU, I was shifted to ward, and he would visit daily to check on my progress both in ICU and in the ward.
Both in ICU and in ward nurses were especially careful with my case thanks to Dr Honnekeri attention.

I could see that all the staff respects him tremendously thanks to his prodigious knowledge and willingness to explain to them why he wants certain things done in a particular way.

His attention to detail is second to none and especially, he focuses on preparing the patient pre-surgery and personally attends to all post-operative care such as monitoring your vitals, medications and dosage being given to you, and post-operative bandaging and wound care.

During pre-surgery preparations he emphasized that I regularly practice deep breathing using the spirometer, and that this helps during surgery and in post-surgery recovery.

I followed his advice to the T and just within 2 weeks of discharge from the hospital, I am able to walk 25 minutes twice a day each time covering a distance of 1.5 km each. I am also able to attend to my office work remotely, occasionally attending long meetings.

After 2 weeks of discharge, I am on my last leg of bandage care and the primary wound is healing well.

I feel Dr Honnekeri is as close to God as possible for giving me a new lease of life.

Along with my immediate family who provided much needed support and care, I deeply thank him for giving me hope and a future. Without him I do not know how things would have turned out.

If you are looking for a cardiac advisor or a surgeon, I highly recommend him. Please do consult with him, it would be the best decision you make in your cardiac recovery!

Our experience with Dr. Tilak Lal was extremely disappointing and has left our family with lasting questions.
On 21st April 2026, we consulted him regarding my mother, a CKD patient under his care. Her nephrologist had specifically advised admission under a cardiologist due to significantly elevated NT-proBNP and Troponin I levels. Despite this, Dr. Tilak Lal repeatedly insisted that her heart was "absolutely fine" and that the problem was entirely kidney-related.
This opinion did not change during the three days she remained hospitalized. No further cardiac investigations were suggested, and our repeated requests and concerns about her heart were consistently dismissed. We were repeatedly given the same assurance that her heart was not the issue.
One month later, my mother suffered a cardiac arrest and passed away.
I understand that no doctor can predict every outcome. However, when a patient presents with elevated cardiac markers and the family repeatedly expresses concern, one would expect a more thorough cardiac evaluation rather than an outright dismissal of the possibility of heart involvement.
What troubles me most is not that my mother could not be saved, but that her cardiac risk did not appear to receive the attention it deserved despite multiple warning signs and repeated requests from the family.
I leave this review because families place enormous trust in specialists, and concerns raised by patients and their caregivers deserve to be carefully considered, especially when significant cardiac markers are involved.

featured_reviews.name: Anuj Saini
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dear All,
Iam a Civil Engineer professional and working with one of the top most construction company in India.
As per company policy, I was asked to undergo a medical checkup referred by the company. These medical checkups are in the panel of the company and I got my tests done from one of the reputed Health experts in Navi Mumbai.

Unfortunately the result turned out to be shocking and a heart blockage was detected.  Being a sports athlete, I couldn't digest the scenario and was shocked & totally devastated.

I was asked to redo the medical test on my own expenditure and confirm to my client if Iam fit for the company.

I happened to call many cardiologists and was lucky enough to get in touch with Dr. BRIJESH AGRAWAL - Cardiologist, Interventional Cardiologist.
Thanks to Ms. Sonal from the receptionist who helped me with  booking the appointment on the spot and solved all my queries. I asked her many questions with respect to the tests done, experience of the doctor, fees etc. I found her professional, smart and quick which made me very comfortable.
Dr. Brijesh Agrawal heart clinic is in Chembur above Malhar Hotel. It was crowded with patients but we were taken inside at the right time slot. inshort, we didn't have to wait for hours like I did in my previous health checkup experience.
Dr. Agrawal is a very knowledgeable and down to earth person.  He is 40+ years old and an interventional cardiologist with more than 15 to 20 years of experience in cardiology, but looks like a teenager :)

He saw all my old reports (2 days old report which shows blockage) and asked me to do a 2D EchoCardiography and Tread mill test.
With the blessings of God, Iam perfectly alright and the previous report turned out to be wrong.
Dr. Brijesh Agrawal explained in detail about Heart functions, how 2D  EchoCardiography would be carried out and I was in total ease before entering the 2D room.
The room was very neat and clean and the equipment looked to be of latest make. I was asked to lay on one side and then a colourless gel was applied to the chest area. Then Dr. Agrawal moved the transducer across the various parts of his chest to get specific/desired views of the heart.
I was happy to see that he was doing it personally and was not dependent on any technician to do it for him.

After 2D Echo I was asked to do Treadmill test wherein I was asked to walk on a treadmill for say 5 minutes.
Before getting onto the treadmill Ms. Sonal and Sister Shivani briefed me how tests would be done and asked me to change the shirt so that the small, flat, sticky white patch can be put on the chest and then electrodes / wire were attached to them. They'll be attached to an electrocardiogram monitor -- called an EKG - that charts your heart's electrical activity during the test.

Within 15 minutes of both the tests being done, I again met Dr. Agrawal with the reports where he declared me fit and fine.  He gave me a fitness certificate which I shall be submitting to my new company !
I was very happy with the service and appreciated the time he gave me and my mother. He explained the entire process of Heart function and was always smiling.

Once again thank you very much Dr. Brijesh Agrwal. I Am very thankful for a quick check up and detailed explanation.

P.s - Incase someone is looking for a good Gynecologist, then I would also suggest to check with Dr. Pradnya Supe who sits in the same clinic.

Regards,
Anuj Saini
